chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn ibn Saeed, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Muhammad ibn Mahfouz, from Ali ibn Al-Nu'man, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Iblis remains joyful as long as the two Muslims desert each other. So when they meet (reconcile), his knees tremble and his joints creak, and he calls out, 'O Woe to me, what I face from the doom!'

key_terms.اهْتَجَرَ: to desert, separate, or cut ties

ai.seo_question: How does the reconciliation between Muslims affect Iblis according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) illustrates the metaphysical reality of Iblis’s rejoicing at Muslim discord, using vivid physical imagery of his knees clashing and joints dislocating upon reconciliation. This highlights the concept of 'ihtijar' (desertion/separation) not merely as a social rift but as a spiritual victory for the enemy, emphasizing that communal unity is a direct cause of Iblis’s distress and eventual ruin.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Saeed, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, from Muhammad Bin Mahfouz, from Ali Bin Al Nu’man, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Iblees<sup>la</sup> does not cease to be joyful for as long as the two Muslims desert each other. So when they meet (reconcile), his<sup>la</sup> knees tremble and his<sup>la</sup> joints creak, and he<sup>la</sup> calls out, ‘O Woe, what I<sup>la</sup> face from the doom!’.
en.sarwar: 7. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sa’id from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Muhammad ibn Mahfuz from Ali ibn al-Nu’man from ibn Muskan from abu Basir from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

As long as two Muslims continue abandoning each other, Satan enjoys it. When they meet, his (Satan’s) knees began to shake and his bone joints began to come apart and he cries, ‘Woe upon me; I have to face this destruction.’”
